The jurisdiction of this Court has been invoked by way of filing an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. at the instance of accused-petitioner.

 and 302 of the IPC and  under Sections 5i, 5j(iv)
 and 6 of the POCSO Act.

5. Offences added, if any Section 376(2)(n) and 306 of the IPC and Section 5(L)(j), 11(iv)/12  of the POCSO Act.

2. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the complainant oppose the bail application and submit that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Government Advocate and the learned counsel for the complainant.

5. After taking into account the submission made at bar and upon consideration of the police report,
as per which, the major part of the FIR lodged at the instance of the complainant Bansi Ram has been found false and it is concluded that the deceased was subjected to rape, upon which, she committed suicide and thus, a case of rape and abatement to commit suicide has been found against the petitioner.
A perusal of the copy of the charge-sheet revealing that the medical evidence blatantly and directly rejecting the possibility of rape.

There is no direct evidence regarding commission of rape and the prosecution has set up the story on the basis of surmises and conjectures only sans any [2023:RJ-JD:39214] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-14397/2023] legally admissible evidence.
As far as the question of abatement given by the petitioner to the deceased to end her life is concerned; there is no direct or indirect evidence except the hypothetical assumption.
The record revealing the presence of poisonous substance at the house of the victim.
At this stage, the plea cannot be ignored that either the deceased was forced to end her life by her parents or she may have committed suicide after receiving taunt or rebuked by her family members.
6. Be that as it may.

After investigation, charge sheet has been filed and of course, the trial would take a long time to reach on a legitimate conclusion and till then keeping the petitioner behind the bars would not be justifiable.
Otherwise also, there are no compelling circumstances for which his further incarceration should be allowed.
In light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
The observation made hereinabove are limited for the justifiable disposal of the bail application which would have no bearance on the merits of the case during the trial.

7. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court [2023:RJ-JD:39214] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-14397/2023] concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

(FARJAND ALI),J 107-divya/-
